headline: Microsoft plans to raise $25 billion in bonds for infrastructure expansion
body: Microsoft announced plans to raise $25 billion in bonds, taking advantage of its healthy credit rating to support infrastructure expansion. Management is targeting $170 billion in 2026 capital expenditures, as the company looks to meet heavy demand from Anthropic and OpenAI, as well as other clients.
note: Microsoft reported positive free cash flow, differentiating itself from Alphabet, Meta and Amazon. Amazon and Alphabet have also turned to the bond market for infrastructure this year.

evidence.text: Microsoft on Thursday announced plans to raise $25 billion in bonds, taking advantage of its healthy credit rating to support its infrastructure expansion.
Management is targeting $170 billion in 2026 capital expenditures, as the company looks to meet heavy demand from artificial intelligence labs Anthropic and OpenAI, as well as other clients.
Microsoft reported positive free cash flow on Wednesday, differentiating itself from Alphabet, whose cash flow was negative for the second quarter in a row.
Last week Meta said it had negative free cash flow, and on Thursday Amazon reported negative free cash flow.
Amazon and Alphabet have engaged the bond market to support infrastructure projects this year, and AI-focused cloud CoreWeave has also relied on the debt market to broaden its data center footprint.
